I have hired finance people in twelve countries, and when somebody tells me a candidate has beautiful English, I always ask what they mean. Because it is almost never the accent. The people whose English I remember as beautiful were clear. They said one thing at a time. They finished their sentences. They stopped talking when they had made their point, and they did not apologize for their accent. A French controller I worked with had a very strong accent and the most elegant English in the building. Beautiful English is not perfect English. It is English that is easy to follow.

I moved to Brazil eight years ago and I learned Portuguese as an adult, so I know the other side of this. For two years I took classes once a week and I did not improve. Then I changed jobs, and I had to speak Portuguese in meetings every day. In three months everything changed. It was like learning to drive. You can read the manual for a year, but you only drive well when you drive every day, and you stop being afraid of the car. Fluency is not something you know. It is something you do, every day, until your mouth stops waiting for your head.
